title: Math Camp
text: A two-week review that prepares incoming PhD students for the O’Neill quantitative sequence, organized into ten one-day modules. Modules 1–6 cover mathematics; modules 7–10 continue into probability and statistics. A third component — the computing workflow used throughout the program — runs alongside.

title: Math Camp
text:
The daily rhythm
Each module is designed to take one day. SPEA 270 is reserved for you for both weeks — you are highly encouraged to work through camp together.



10:00 a.m.
Meet in SPEA 270; work through the module’s lecture notes together


Midday
Attempt the problem set on your own — honest attempts before looking anything up


2:00 p.m.
Reconvene to compare answers and discuss, or do coding assignments


Evening
Review today’s material and read ahead for the next day’s module


Following day
Turn in your handwritten problem set — scan or photograph it and upload it to Canvas; if a problem set involves code, upload your scripts as well



Problem sets are ungraded — they are where the learning happens. The final exam is in person, without AI tools, and is graded.
Alongside the modules, take a look at the Computing Setup and Git & Reproducible Work guides — getting your machine and workflow in shape during camp makes the start of the fall courses much smoother.

title: Probability & Statistics
text:
The second half of camp continues into probability and statistics — the direct on-ramp to V706. Each module runs theory in the morning and computing in the afternoon.
The Slides column lists every deck for that day: the M-deck is the morning theory session and the W-deck is the afternoon computing session. Module 7 also lists W1, the install-and-setup deck to work through before camp starts, and module 9 carries a short evening deck (M4) on the named distributions.

NoteHow to use these modules



Work the modules in order — each builds on the previous. Readings for each module are listed in the syllabus. Write your own R rather than having it written for you. The bugs and the error messages are the curriculum, not an obstacle to it.


Get R and RStudio installed before Module 7: start with W2 and the Computing Setup guide. The full computing track, including Git, is on the Workflow & Coding page.
Reference: Bruce E. Hansen, Probability and Statistics for Economists (Princeton University Press, 2021) — chapters 1–3, 6–7.
